## Purpose and Entry Points
Bifrost is a Go-based AI gateway that normalizes inference across many LLM and multimodal providers behind OpenAI-compatible and provider-compatible HTTP APIs. It can also be embedded as a Go SDK.
- HTTP server executable: `transports/bifrost-http/main.go`
- Core SDK façade: `core/bifrost.go`
- Interactive/local CLI: `cli/main.go`
- Browser administration UI is a separate TypeScript application served by the gateway: `ui/app/main.tsx`, `transports/bifrost-http/handlers/ui.go`

## HTTP Gateway and API Compatibility
The HTTP transport owns server initialization, routing, authentication/middleware, request validation, streaming/websocket handling, inference endpoints, and management APIs. It is the boundary between external clients and the core runtime.
- Server composition and lifecycle: `transports/bifrost-http/server/server.go`
- Canonical inference request handlers: `transports/bifrost-http/handlers/inference.go`
- SDK-compatibility routing for OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, GenAI, LangChain, LiteLLM, and others: `transports/bifrost-http/integrations/router.go`, `transports/bifrost-http/integrations/openai.go`
- Public API contract is maintained under `docs/openapi/openapi.yaml` and `docs/openapi/paths/inference/`

## Core Inference Runtime
`core` defines shared schemas and orchestrates request execution. It transforms normalized requests into provider-specific API calls, selects configured keys, handles errors/streams, and returns normalized responses. Provider modules implement the external-service boundary rather than exposing provider details to transport callers.
- Primary runtime and shared API: `core/bifrost.go`, `core/schemas/bifrost.go`
- Provider interface/schema layer: `core/schemas/provider.go`
- Representative provider adapters: `core/providers/openai/openai.go`, `core/providers/anthropic/anthropic.go`, `core/providers/bedrock/bedrock.go`
- Streaming and provider HTTP utilities: `core/providers/utils/stream.go`, `core/network/http.go`

## Plugin Pipeline, Routing, and Governance
Plugins are a first-class interception boundary around inference and MCP operations. The core pipeline loads configured plugins; plugins can implement request policy, routing, caching, logging, telemetry, mocking, or compatibility behavior without embedding those concerns in providers.
- Pipeline and plugin interfaces: `core/mcp/pluginpipeline.go`, `core/schemas/plugin.go`
- Dynamic/native plugin loading: `framework/plugins/loader.go`, `framework/plugins/soloader.go`
- Governance applies virtual-key, budget, rate-limit, complexity, and routing policies: `plugins/governance/main.go`, `plugins/governance/routing.go`
- Built-in semantic caching uses vector stores: `plugins/semanticcache/main.go`, `plugins/semanticcache/search.go`

## MCP Gateway
Bifrost can manage MCP clients/servers, discover and filter tools, execute tools, maintain sessions, and support agent/code modes. MCP credentials are isolated behind credential-store implementations, including per-user headers and OAuth.
- MCP initialization and client orchestration: `core/mcp/init.go`, `core/mcp/clientmanager.go`
- Tool inventory/execution: `core/mcp/toolmanager.go`, `core/mcp/exec.go`
- Agent and code-mode behavior: `core/mcp/agent.go`, `core/mcp/codemode.go`
- HTTP MCP, sessions, and OAuth surfaces: `transports/bifrost-http/handlers/mcp.go`, `transports/bifrost-http/handlers/mcpoauth2.go`

## Persistence, Catalogs, and Observability
The optional framework layer abstracts operational state from inference execution. It supports SQLite/Postgres configuration and logs, ClickHouse logs, object storage, model/pricing catalogs, and vector-backed semantic cache. This permits zero-config/in-memory-style operation or durable production deployment.
- Config state, migrations, and secret-related persistence: `framework/configstore/store.go`, `framework/configstore/migrations.go`
- Request/usage log storage: `framework/logstore/store.go`, `framework/logstore/clickhouse.go`
- Model catalog and pricing synchronization: `framework/modelcatalog/main.go`, `framework/modelcatalog/datasheet/sync.go`
- Storage integrations: `framework/vectorstore/store.go`, `framework/objectstore/s3.go`, `framework/objectstore/gcs.go`

## Operations and Deployment
The primary runtime is Go; the admin UI is TypeScript/React-style frontend code. Deployment targets include Docker, Kubernetes/Helm, and Terraform for AWS, Azure, GCP, and generic Kubernetes. External dependencies commonly include LLM provider APIs, PostgreSQL/SQLite, ClickHouse, Redis, Qdrant, Weaviate, Pinecone, S3/GCS, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry collectors.
- Container build/runtime: `transports/Dockerfile`, `transports/docker-entrypoint.sh`
- Helm deployment plus optional PostgreSQL/Redis/Qdrant/Weaviate: `helm-charts/bifrost/templates/deployment.yaml`, `helm-charts/bifrost/values.yaml`
- Cloud and Kubernetes provisioning modules: `terraform/modules/bifrost/main.tf`
